proof.text: Realize $\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ as module sheaves on the diagram site of the one-object point site with constant ring $R$, using [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] with $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. It is a small ringed site, so [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] gives the derived tensor-Hom bijection there. For a K-flat representative $P$ of $C$, its constant tower is K-flat: tensoring it with an acyclic tower is acyclic at every level, hence acyclic by levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. For a K-injective resolution $I_\bullet$ of $A_\bullet$, the internal Hom from $\operatorname{const}P$ is exactly the tower $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_R(P,I_n)$. Indeed the slice at $n$ has objects $1,\ldots,n$; a natural map from a constant module to the restricted tower is determined by its component at $n$, and its component at $i\le n$ is transition composed with that component. This applies to every degree of the Hom complex and its differential. Evaluation of $I_\bullet$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective]. Thus this internal Hom is the specified $\mathsf J(C)$ and evaluates to $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n)$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, mapping complexes before limits; ringed-site realization and tensor-Hom transposition (Stacks Tags 08J9 and 0FPT).

proof.text:
Write $\lambda_K=t\circ\beta_K\circ(1\otimes\eta_K)$. Its three factors are morphisms of the derived tower category: the pairing is supplied by [lem-coef-tower-evaluation-pairing], the coaugmentation by [lem-coef-tower-coaugmentation], and $t$ is the single fixed lift in the hypothesis. Define $\Gamma_K$ to be the image of $\lambda_K$ under the tensor-Hom bijection of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. By its evaluation normalization,
$$e_C\circ(\Gamma_K\otimes1_{\operatorname{const}C})=\lambda_K,$$
where $e_C:\mathsf J(C)\otimes_R^L\operatorname{const}C\to A_\bullet$ is evaluation. On the representatives in step 1, this counit sends a homogeneous map and its argument to their ordinary evaluation; its component at $n$ is the counit for $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n)$. Tensor is also evaluated termwise: for a K-flat tower $T$ and an acyclic $R$-complex $V$, $T\otimes\operatorname{const}V$ is acyclic, hence each $T_n\otimes V$ is acyclic; thus every $T_n$ is K-flat. Quasi-isomorphisms are levelwise. Consequently $\operatorname{ev}_n\Gamma_K$ is the transpose of $\operatorname{ev}_n\lambda_K$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, the middle mapping-complex comparison and its specified natural maps.

proof.text: Fix $n\ge1$. Put $H_n=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,\omega_n)$ and $D_n=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C_n,A_n)$, regarded also as $R$-complexes by restriction. The evaluation-pairing node identifies $\operatorname{ev}_n\mathsf H(K)=H_n$ and $\operatorname{ev}_nB_K=C_n$ and identifies the evaluated pairing with compact-support projection followed by evaluation. The fixed trace evaluates to the finite exceptional counit. Moreover $K_n$ is bounded constructible by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and has the assumed finite Tor interval. Hence [lem-coef-finite-mapping-adjunction] applies to $M=K_n$ and gives the isomorphism $\gamma_{n,K_n}:H_n\to D_n$, whose transpose is exactly projection, evaluation and this counit. These are the same maps specified in the item, with the same compactification and finite exceptional comparison functor; no ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint is used.

source.place: Paragraph 2, finite exceptional adjunction on mapping complexes.

proof.text:
Let $q_n:C\to\operatorname{Res}C_n$ be $\operatorname{ev}_n\eta_K$. By [lem-coef-tower-coaugmentation] its scalar-extension adjunct is the canonical isomorphism $\theta_n:C\otimes_R^LA_n\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction] on the one-object point site to $R\to A_n$, $K=C$, $N=A_n$. It gives the evaluation-normalized isomorphism
$$\alpha_n:\operatorname{Res}\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C\otimes_R^LA_n,A_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n).$$
The composite $\alpha_n\circ\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(\theta_n,A_n)\circ\gamma_{n,K_n}$ has transpose the finite projection/evaluation/counit pairing precomposed in its second variable by $q_n$. In fact the scalar-adjunction node normalizes its transpose by the unit $u_n:C\to\operatorname{Res}(C\otimes_R^LA_n)$, and $q_n=(\operatorname{Res}\theta_n)u_n$ by the adjunct formula. Step 3 and the evaluated pairing identify that precomposed pairing with $\operatorname{ev}_n\lambda_K$. Bijectivity of tensor-Hom transposition therefore identifies the displayed composite with $\operatorname{ev}_n\Gamma_K$, proving the asserted finite evaluation formula.

source.place: Paragraph 2, third displayed line: derived scalar adjunction with the actual compact-support projection.

proof.text: Every map in the evaluation formula of step 4 is an isomorphism: $\gamma_{n,K_n}$ by finite mapping adjunction, precomposition by $\theta_n$ because $\theta_n$ is an isomorphism, and $\alpha_n$ by scalar adjunction. Thus every $\operatorname{ev}_n\Gamma_K$ is an isomorphism. Apply the isomorphism-detection clause of [lem-weil-pbc-sequential-tower-evaluation-full] to the already constructed tower morphism $\Gamma_K$ on the point site with ring $R$. It follows that $\Gamma_K$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$. Only detection is used here; no lift or uniqueness assertion is used to construct $\Gamma_K$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, the second and third mapping-complex isomorphisms before total inverse limit.

proof.text:
For $f:K\to K'$, write $h=\mathsf H(f)$, $b=B(f)$ and $c=\operatorname{const}C(f)$. The dinaturality statement of [lem-coef-tower-evaluation-pairing] says $\beta_K(h\otimes1)=\beta_{K'}(1\otimes b)$ as actual derived tower morphisms. Naturality of [lem-coef-tower-coaugmentation] says $b\eta_K=\eta_{K'}c$. Functoriality of tensor and associativity of composition give
$$\begin{aligned}
\lambda_K(h\otimes1)&=t\beta_K(h\otimes\eta_K)\\
&=t\beta_{K'}(1\otimes b)(1\otimes\eta_K)\\
&=t\beta_{K'}(1\otimes\eta_{K'}c)\\
&=\lambda_{K'}(1\otimes c).
\end{aligned}$$
The same $t$ occurs throughout, since it was fixed independently of $K$. This proves an equality before evaluation in the index direction.

source.place: Final paragraph, all four lines identify the specified natural maps; naturality before inverse limits.

proof.text:
Transpose the two equal maps in step 6 using the bijection of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], with source $\mathsf H(K')\otimes_R^L\operatorname{const}C$ and target $A_\bullet$. Naturality in the first tensor variable makes the transpose of $\lambda_K(h\otimes1)$ equal to $\Gamma_Kh$. Naturality in its second variable makes the transpose of $\lambda_{K'}(1\otimes c)$ equal to $\mathsf J(C(f))\Gamma_{K'}$. Their equality is precisely
$$\mathsf J(C(f))\circ\Gamma_{K'}=\Gamma_K\circ\mathsf H(f).$$
It holds in the derived tower category itself, as required.

source.place: Final paragraph, naturality of the specified mapping-complex comparison.

title: Natural tower currying isomorphism
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use ordinary module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, with completed coefficient sheaf $R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ for $W=X,s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $F_n=Ra_{!,n}$ for compact support using one fixed compactification $a=pj$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], $G_n=Ra_n^!$ for the finite constructible comparison-class exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and $\omega_n=G_n(A_n)_s$. Fix a strict complex $Q_\bullet$ of $(A_n)_X$-modules with quotient-semilinear transitions, representing a normalized dualizing tower [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]: $Q_n$ represents $\omega_n$, and its transitions are adjoint to the counit-defined comparisons $\omega_m\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\cong\omega_n$ of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and suppose its reductions have Tor amplitude in one finite interval $[a_0,b_0]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $C_n=\Gamma(s,F_nK_n)$ and $C=\Gamma(s,Ra_!K)$, with coefficient-point sections [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Suppose $\dim X\le d$ for an integer $d\ge0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathsf H(K),B_K,B_\omega$ and $\beta_K$ be the specified derived towers and dinatural pairing of [lem-coef-tower-evaluation-pairing]. Fix a trace $t:B_\omega\to A_\bullet$ evaluating to the finite counits, independently of $K$, using the compatible finite counits of [lem-coef-tower-trace-rectification] and the lift of [lem-weil-pbc-sequential-tower-evaluation-full]. Let $\eta_K:\operatorname{const}C\to B_K$ be the natural coaugmentation of [lem-coef-tower-coaugmentation]. Define $\mathsf J(C)$ to be the derived tower Hom from $\operatorname{const}C$ to $A_\bullet$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; it is computed by termwise Hom from a constant K-flat representative of $C$ into a K-injective resolution of the whole tower $A_\bullet$. Thus $\operatorname{ev}_n\mathsf J(C)=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n)$.
Currying the composite
$$\mathsf H(K)\otimes_R^L\operatorname{const}C\xrightarrow{1\otimes\eta_K}\mathsf H(K)\otimes_R^LB_K\xrightarrow{\beta_K}B_\omega\xrightarrow{t}A_\bullet$$
gives an isomorphism $\Gamma_K:\mathsf H(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf J(C)$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$. Its evaluation at $n$ is $\gamma_{n,K_n}$ of [lem-coef-finite-mapping-adjunction] followed by the canonical scalar-adjunction isomorphism $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C_n,A_n)\cong\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n)$. For every $f:K\to K'$ with induced $C(f):C\to C'$, the equality $\mathsf J(C(f))\circ\Gamma_{K'}=\Gamma_K\circ\mathsf H(f)$ holds in the derived tower category.
